# Copyright 2026 Saimonokuma. Part of RoT DTD GOAL.
# Every LAW.n declared in hooks/trust_contract.dtd must appear here with the
# name of a test case that CAN FAIL if the law is broken. test_every_law_is
# _enforced checks both directions: no law without a test, no named test that
# does not exist in tests/run_tests.sh. A principle nobody can falsify is a
# slogan, and this file is what stops the SOUL section from becoming one.
# The third column is a real case name, not a description. Run it:

what breaking it would look like »: the gate completes on a criterion that never ran, or on text rather than an exit code
a criterion is edited under a live goal and the ledger still audits clean
the block message re-feeds the whole goal instead of the failing criteria
the budget is exhausted and the loop keeps going instead of escalating
state becomes a binary blob, or a decision reads something not on disk
a script reaches for python, jq, or a language runtime

statement: Instruments can fail and never lie reassuringly
what breaking it would look like »: an alarm that cannot be tripped on purpose, or one that hides a real finding
an event is wired with no consumer and no forensic classification

statement: A pass is evidence only if reproducible
what breaking it would look like »: a criterion that regressed still counts as passing evidence

statement: Nothing on the label may be typed
what breaking it would look like »: a count is typed into README or REVIEW instead of generated

statement: No decision is made from a clock
what breaking it would look like »: a backwards clock changes a verdict, or a decision compares timestamps
a criterion prints GOAL COMPLETE and it reaches the reader unfenced

statement: A queued goal starts only after its predecessor was verified
what breaking it would look like »: a dependent goal starts while its predecessor is unfinished

statement: A grammar is declared once and read by the code that enforces it
what breaking it would look like »: narrowing the declared grammar changes nothing about what is accepted

statement: An on-disk record is append-only: field numbers are dense, never reused, never reordered.
what breaking it would look like »: A file grows a column, an old reader keeps parsing it, and $4 quietly means something else. The check that asserted "four columns" expires into a snapshot and gets deleted.

statement: An agent may only speak in a declared element, and every declared agent exists.
what breaking it would look like »: An agent file nobody declared, or a declaration with no file. Its prose then reads as official without any test binding it to the contract.

statement: A refusal always carries a task -- the gate blocks with the next step, never with a wall.
what breaking it would look like »: A message that says COMPLETION REFUSED and nothing else. The agent stops trying, which is the built-in loop failure this engine exists to replace.

statement: A gate that runs out of time blocks and says so -- a slow pipeline costs an iteration, never a verdict.
what breaking it would look like »: the completion pipeline outlives the Stop hook timeout, the harness kills the hook, and the session ends with no verdict at all -- measured in bench 2, 300 seconds to the second.
